She grows up in the home of the mayor of Colchester, whose younger son Robert is her first husband, but he dies after five years. The only man she truly loves, Jemy, parts ways with her, but she meets him again in prison and spends her declining years with him on a plantation inherited from her mother. Her novel's title refers to her as "Twelve Year a Whore, five times a Wife (whereof once to her own brother), Twelve Year a Thief, and Eight Year a Transported Felon in Virginia." FTP, name this title character of a novel by Daniel Defoe.

text: One of this poet's works begins by asking Miranda to "Take this slave of music," and is entitled "To a Lady, With a Guitar," while he lamented that "love should be a blight and snare" in his poem "The Revolt of Islam." This poet described "The Spirit of Solitude" in his poem about the titular Last Man, Alastor. He noted that "the everlasting universe of things flows through the mind" in "Mont Blanc," while in a better known poem, this poet asked the "most musical of mourners" to "weep anew." Those lines come from this poet's elegy for John Keats, "Adonais", and he asked "If Winter Comes, can Spring be far behind?" in a poem written to "the breath of Autumn's being." For ten points, identify this poet who wrote "Ode to the West Wind" and described a crumbling monument in his "Ozymandias."

text: In a novel, the father of this writer befriends a hermit in a cave near Gouda, later becoming that city's vicar. The title character of a dialogue by this author justifies pursuing wealth because Aristotle ordered the goods of fortune before the goods of the mind and is mocked by being given the title Pestiferous Maximus. Margaret Brandt and Gerard Eliassoen are revealed to have been the parents of this man in Charles Reade's novel The Cloister and the Hearth. He wrote an essay about an offspring of Plutus and Freshness whose name is sometimes translated to refer to his friend and collaborator, Thomas More. For 10 points, name this author of Julius Exclusus, a Dutch humanist who also wrote In Praise of Folly.

text: One character in this novel is greatly affected by a photograph in a Life coffee-table book in which she is on her way home from school with Lydia, who is carrying her bag. That character criticizes the title character for abandoning his lover Ellen, after which he takes control of the truck that had been given to another character for his 40th birthday. That character is additionally maddened by Daniel, who, after teaching the title character how to drive the truck, steals his gun while the others are gathered around a music box. The children, Gina, Victor, and Royce, easily adjust to their new life, while in the end one of their parents abandons them to run after a helicopter, hoping to escape the racial violence that originally forced the Smales family to join the village of their servant, the title character. For 10 points name this novel set in revolution-torn South Africa by Nadine Gordimer.

text: One member of this family imagines a giant, black harpy bearing down on him and repeatedly pictures himself stabbing his father. That character is upset when a dinner guest asks for a second bowl of soup. A third member of this family worries that repairs to a greenhouse will cost fifty pounds. Its members Prue and Andrew die of childbirth and in World War I. Its youngest children Cam and James undertake a trip by boat with their father in the last section of the novel. For 10 points, name this family that appears alongside Lily Briscoe in Virginia Woolf's novel To The Lighthouse.
